verses.text: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year that Jehoshaphat was king of Judah. He ruled for twelve years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, but not as much as his father and mother had done. He got rid of the sacred stone pillar of Baal that his father had made.
But he kept on doing the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin. He did not turn away from them.
Mesha king of Moab raised sheep. Every year he had to pay the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.
But after Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
So at that time King Joram went out from Samaria and called up all Israel for war.

He also sent a message to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?" Jehoshaphat answered, "I will go. I am with you all the way. My people are your people, and my horses are your horses."
Then he asked, "Which way should we attack?" Joram answered, "Through the desert of Edom."
So the king of Israel set out with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. After they had marched around for seven days, there was no water left for the army or for the animals with them.
The king of Israel cried, "Oh no! The LORD has brought us three kings together only to hand us over to Moab!"

But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there not a prophet of the LORD here, so we can ask the LORD through him?" One of the king of Israel's officials answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He used to pour water on Elijah's hands."
Jehoshaphat said, "The LORD's word is with him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to see him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What do you want with me? Go to the prophets of your father and mother." The king of Israel answered, "No, because it is the LORD who has brought us three kings together to hand us over to Moab."
Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD of Armies lives, the God I serve, if I did not respect Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not even look at you or notice you.
But now bring me someone who plays the harp." While the harpist was playing, the LORD's power came on Elisha.
He said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Dig ditches all over this valley.'
The LORD says, 'You will not see wind or rain, but this valley will be filled with water. Then you, your cattle, and your other animals will drink.'
This is an easy thing for the LORD. He will also hand Moab over to you.
You will conquer every walled city and every important town. You will cut down every good tree, block up all the springs, and ruin every good field by covering it with stones."
The next morning, about the time of the morning sacrifice, water came flowing from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
Meanwhile, all the people of Moab had heard that the kings had come to fight against them. So everyone old enough to put on armour, young and old, was called up and stationed at the border.
When they got up early the next morning, the sun was shining on the water. To the Moabites across the valley, the water looked as red as blood.
They said, "That is blood! The kings must have fought and killed each other. Now, Moab, let's go and take what they left behind!"
But when the Moabites came to Israel's camp, the Israelites rose up and attacked them, and they ran away. The Israelites pushed on into the land, killing the Moabites.

They destroyed the towns. Each man threw a stone onto every good field until it was covered. They blocked up all the springs and cut down all the good trees. Only Kir Hareseth was left with its stone walls standing, but men with slings surrounded it and attacked it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was going against him, he took seven hundred swordsmen with him to try to break through to the king of Edom, but they failed.
Then he took his oldest son, who was to be king after him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall. Great anger came against Israel, so they left him and went back to their own land.
